newsitem.title: USA: FGIC says Q4 net income fell 25.9 pct to $41.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: FGIC says Q4 net income fell 25.9 pct to $41.4 mln.

text.p: Financial Guaranty Insurance Co, a unit of GE Capital Services, said Wednesday its fourth quarter net income fell 25.9 percent to $41.4 million from $55.9 million in the last quarter of 1995.
For the full year, net income dropped to $177.6 million from $187.9 million, FGIC said. GE Capital Services is a unit of General Electric Co.
In a statement announcing the results, the company said its 1996 volume increased, and it took the lead in sectors it has decided to continue insuring.

"The processes and practices designed make FGIC the low-cost, customer-driven bond insurer were fixed firmly in place in 1996, assuring FGIC's competitive advantage and its long-term vitality," Ann Stern, FGIC's chairman, president and chief executive officer, said.
Stern said FGIC is positioned to grow in 1997 through product development and diversification into other markets and businesses.
The company also said it captured the number one market share spot in general obligation bonds, and the number two spot in both water and sewer bonds and transportation bonds.
FGIC said total revenues rose in 1996 to $258.6 million from $256.4 million.
Core net income rose to $156.6 million from $155.9 million.
